d.d: A member of an oligarchy; someone who is part of a small group that runs a country.
A very wealthy business owner who wields political power.
A protoplanet formed during oligarchic accretion.
Of or pertaining to oligarchy.
plural of oligarch
A government run by and for only a few, often the aristocracy, the wealthy, or their friends and associates.
A state ruled by such a government.
d.x: The 1832 Reform Act aimed to transform the British oligarchy and allow Parliament to represent the interests of a broader range of the population.

d.d: Those who make up an oligarchic government.
d.x: The modern British oligarchy—particularly during periods of Tory rule—has been called a chumocracy.

d.d: Of a geologic epoch within the Paleogene period from about 34 to 23 million years ago; marked by the rapid evolution in a warm climate.
plural of oligomer

plural of oligonucleotide
An economic condition in which a small number of sellers exert control over the market of a commodity.
plural of oligosaccharide
A rich, thick, Spanish stew consisting of meat and vegetables.
A medley or mixture; a hotchpotch.
A collection of various musical, theatrical or other artistic works; a miscellany.
An ancient ivory hunting-horn.
olivary body
